text: You're online, adding items to your shopping cart. Suddenly, something pulls you away – a call, or you just need to think. You close the tab.
A day later, you remember those items. You open the site, expecting to start over. But there it is: your cart, perfectly preserved, waiting.
It feels like magic, or just good service. You might wonder if it's a cookie, or if the website knew you'd return.
This isn't magic. It's a persistent user state, linking your session to an anonymous or logged-in profile. The system remembers your specific choices.
This convenience removes friction, making it easier to complete your purchase. But it means the store tracks your intent, sending subtle nudges.
So the next time your cart is waiting, remember: it’s not just memory; it’s a quiet, engineered system designed to help you and the seller complete the transaction.
